finding: Patient tests' drain limit equals their own 60 s wait, so a gate that admits requests during the drain is caught late
evidence: patient_server sets drain_within = close_within = BROKEN_AFTER (60 s), the same limit wait_until_closing uses; I mutated lifecycle::gate to refuse only at `== Phase::Closing`; only a_request_whose_body_arrives_during_the_drain_still_gets_its_reply failed, after 60 s; the other patient tests passed after 60 s; requests_while_closing_get_503 checks only the Closing phase.

finding: A body finishing right as a timed-out drain ends can start its call only 25 ms before the quit work begins
evidence: routes::api reads the phase as Draining, then run() stores Closing and sleeps 25 ms before backend.quit(); the call then overlaps the quit work like a call that outlasts the drain, while the old rule gave every started call the full drain (check-then-act window, lib.rs:309-317, routes.rs:158).

finding: Each card read lists the whole projects folder again
evidence: `peek` and `summary_files` both call `listed()` (store.rs:362, 389), which reads the whole projects folder. A Home visit with N cards therefore lists it N+1 times, plus once per `home/card` read, where §4.5 says 'one listing and one stat per card'.

finding: A panic in the HomeSummary job stops every later summary this launch
evidence: `summary_done` (home.rs:570) runs only when the job returns normally. If the job panics, `running` stays set, `start_next` never starts another job, and every card shows "—" until the app restarts.
